I am a PhD student in the Department of Political Science at the University of California San Diego.

I study comparative politics and the political economy of development, with a regional focus on Turkey, MENA, and Southeastern Europe. My current research examines how governments build electoral support through distributive programs, including social assistance, subsidized public services, and credit. I also work on the historical political economy of state building in the late Ottoman Empire. Methodologically, I use causal inference for observational data, experimental methods, LLM-based archival data extraction, and geospatial analysis. I am also developing a specialization in formal theory.
